name: cross-engine-coupling
title: Cross-engine coupling: engines are interchangeable at a seam
question: Can one composite run part of the model in one engine and part in another (libroadrunner, COPASI, or the native process), sharing one store - a composition a monolithic SBML model structurally cannot express - and are the engines interchangeable at the seam?
hypothesis: A hybrid composite (upper glycolysis in Tellurium, lower glycolysis in COPASI or the native process) sharing one species store runs through process-bigraph and reproduces the biological-seam result - the engine at either side of the seam is a drop-in, the composability payoff a monolith can never match.
objective: Demonstrate cross-engine composition impossible for a monolith, and that engines are swappable at a seam - the existence proof for the composability axis.
description: Study in the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. cross-engine-coupling swaps biological-modular-seam's lower-glycolysis submodel for the native-pbg process while upper stays libroadrunner, both sharing one store. This is the composability existence proof; it has no monolithic reference (accuracy-exempt). The generic reaction_split composite makes the engine a parameter of each side of the seam: the baseline couples Tellurium (upper) with COPASI (lower); the native-lower variant couples Tellurium with the hand-ported native process. Both reproduce the Tellurium+Tellurium biological-seam result at the same coupling interval to ~3e-7 (measured below).
claim: A single composite runs HALF in one engine and HALF in another, sharing one store - structurally impossible for a monolith. Swapping the lower half of the seam=aldolase composite from Tellurium to COPASI or to the native process reproduces the Tellurium+Tellurium trajectory at the same coupling interval (0.005) to max relative error 3.2e-7 (COPASI 3.19e-7, native 3.20e-7, measured); the engines are interchangeable at a seam as a ~1e-7 drop-in (COPASI is not bit-reproducible run to run). This is the composability payoff, not a numeric result.

expected_behavior.name: cross-engine-composition-runs
expected_behavior.observable: a two-engine composite running through process-bigraph
expected_behavior.condition: builds, runs, emits the full 17-species set with finite output; accuracy-exempt (no monolithic reference)
expected_behavior.rationale: the value is the structural capability, demonstrated by a working cross-engine composite, not a trajectory match.

findings.summary: Hybrid composite: upper glycolysis (Tellurium SubmodelProcess) + lower glycolysis (NativeSubmodelProcess) share one species store, reconciling additively — a composition a single libroadrunner model cannot express.

Matches the Tellurium+Tellurium reference at the same interval (0.005) when the lower half is swapped (same ODEs, different engine): max_rel_err 3.19e-7 for the COPASI swap, 3.20e-7 for the native swap; the monolith-impossibility is STRUCTURAL, not numeric. Accuracy-exempt in the 3-way figure.

Engine interchangeability is measured on both swaps (seam=aldolase, interval 0.005, vs tellurium+tellurium): tellurium+COPASI 3.19e-7, tellurium+native 3.20e-7. Both are ~1e-7 engine-swap drop-ins; COPASI is not bit-reproducible and varies at the ~1e-7 level run to run.
